## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Score Reporting
• Two words that flow off the tongue and promise so much but
mean so little.
• What are we talking about when we discuss a “score report”?
• What is the purpose of a score report (I know, to “report
scores” 😂)
• How would we distinguish a “good” score report from a
“bad” score report?
• To answer these questions well we need to get out our scalpel
and do some hair splitting.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Score Reporting
• What do we mean by scores:
• Let’s not make this too hard! We’ll focus on education
related “scores”.
• I’d argue that scores can be quantitative or qualitative - no
need to nitpick over what is and isn’t a score.
• These scores are presumably reported by means of a
“report”</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/06.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Score Reporting
• What do we mean by reporting:
• This is where is gets more sticky.
• A report presumably communicates/explains something
(scores and their interpretations) to “someone”
• Most often the someone is/are human being(s)
• However, score reporting can take place between
“machines” via APIs for machine consumption.
• We’ll focus on score reporting for people.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/11.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Hard Questions
• Some of the dumbest questions are the hardest questions to answer.
• And REAL answers to these dumb questions are necessary to make good
score reports:
• Who is the report for?
• How do we intend the users to use the scores?
• What do we think will occur if the users use the scores as we intend?
• What outcomes do we think will follow the use of the scores (as we
intend).
• The difference between good and bad score reporting will center on how
well we carry out the labor intensive work of score reporting design.</div>
```
